sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16-tsingmicro-FlagOS - Hugging Face
sources.snippet: Introduction On August 26, Alibaba open-sourced its multimodal MoE model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. The FlagOS community completed Day-0 synchronized adaptation across multiple chips, having accomplished multi-chip adaptation, precision alignment, and deployment validation based on the FlagOS unified open-source technology stack on 8 AI chips — including T-Head (Pingtouge), NVIDIA, Moore Threads ...

sources.title: FlagRelease/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16-zhenwu-FlagOS · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is regarded as an early preview of the Qwen4 architecture. It introduces systematic upgrades across four areas—attention, residuals, embedding, and the optimizer—enhancing the model's capabilities while further optimizing computational efficiency, model capacity, and training stability.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next - GitHub
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next features a 125B -parameter main model, supplemented by an additional 51B N-gram embeddings, with 6B parameters activated per token. Compared with Qwen3.7-Plus, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next substantially reduces both training and inference cost — training takes only about 1/9 as much, yet it delivers superior capabilities in coding and office tasks.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: How to Run Locally - unsloth.ai
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a new open-weight, 125B parameter MoE multimodal model from Qwen. Built on the new Qwen4 architecture, it supports a 262K context window and advanced reasoning.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next - SGLang Documentation
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model released as an early preview of the architecture Qwen4 is being built on — the same role Qwen3-Next played for Qwen3.5, whose hybrid Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention design then carried through the Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3.7 and Qwen3.8 series.
